title: These startups hope “blended” food will cut our appetite for red meat
gist: Fully plant-based meat (Impossible, Beyond) has stalled: category sales fell 10% in 2025 while US beef consumption rose 4.3% to $45 billion. Startups are now pitching 'blended' meat, meaning beef mixed with mushrooms or mycelium, as the realistic way to cut red-meat emissions. Joyn's 50/Cut is in school cafeterias in seven states at a 5-15% discount to beef, with half the GHG footprint of a beef patty. Backers frame it as a pleasure-first 'hybrid car' bridge, while skeptics expect the impact to stay mostly in institutional dining.

themes.theme: Why diet change is unavoidable for climate

insights.claim: Livestock accounts for 10-20% of human-caused greenhouse-gas emissions, nearly two-thirds of it from ruminants. Beef herds emit four times as much as dairy herds per kilo of food, and ruminants produce about 30% of human-related methane.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Beef is the biggest emissions lever in food, so it is the obvious target for regulation, carbon pricing or substitution.

insights.claim: Chalmers professor Fredrik Hedenus says that even if fossil fuel use stopped tomorrow, agricultural emissions would push warming past 2 °C by 2070. More efficient livestock farming would still leave agriculture using over half of humanity's carbon budget, and only diet change produces a winning scenario in his model.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: There is no technical fix for ruminant digestion, so climate policy will eventually have to address what people eat.
insights.quote: “We don’t have a technical solution to change the stomach of a rumina
insights.locator: Even if the world stopped burning

insights.claim: Cultural resistance to eating less meat is entrenched: global meat production quadrupled between 1961 and 2022, meat-eating rises with wealth and status, and US vegetarianism has held at about 4% since 1999.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Demand-side strategies that need people to change their preferences have a poor base rate, so favor products that fit existing habits.
insights.locator: Yet the culture has proved intractable

themes.theme: Collapse of the plant-based meat thesis

insights.claim: Plant-based meat has gone from hype to decline. Beyond's 2019 IPO was the most successful since 2008, but by 2023 Impossible employees' stock values had fallen 89% from their 2021 high, Beyond had cut 20% of staff, and category sales dropped 10% year over year in 2025, according to the Good Food Institute.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: The fully plant-based category is in structural decline, so be wary of rebound theses for Beyond or Impossible.

insights.claim: Americans bought $45 billion of beef in 2025 and consumption rose 4.3% from the year before, according to an industry report. Rising prices may slow that only modestly.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Beef demand is resilient even at high prices, which supports pricing power for beef packers.

insights.claim: Nectar's research finds that consumers report bad aftertaste and off flavors in plant-based meats five to six times more often than in the animal versions, making sensory quality a main barrier to adoption.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Taste, not price or virtue, is the binding constraint, so judge alt-protein bets on how they perform in sensory tests.

insights.locator: Nectar, an organization that conducts research

insights.claim: The 'ultra-processed' label, first pushed by the meat-industry-backed Center for Consumer Freedom in 2019, has become a political weapon for the MAHA movement and HHS Secretary RFK Jr., who flipped the food pyramid in 2025 to put steak on top. That has damaged plant-based meat's reputation.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: US policy is currently hostile to processed meat alternatives, a regulatory and narrative headwind for the category.

themes.theme: Blended meat as the pragmatic substitute

insights.claim: BMC Ingredients cofounder Paul Shapiro argues that if Impossible Whoppers are about 2% of Burger King sales, that cuts meat by only 2%, whereas making every conventional Whopper 20% plants would cut meat 20% immediately. Partial substitution across all volume beats full substitution in a niche.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Penetrating the existing base with a small share beats a niche replacement, which favors ingredient suppliers selling into incumbents.
insights.locator: Paul Shapiro, cofounder of the startup

insights.claim: A 2022 Nature study found that replacing 20% of beef globally could halve the annual rate of deforestation.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Modest partial substitution has outsized land-use effects, which is relevant to deforestation-linked ESG and supply-chain rules.
insights.locator: Those aren’t quite the numbers climate models

insights.claim: Consumers accept blended meat: a USDA co-funded blind taste test in 2022 found diners preferred blended burgers to fully plant-based ones, and an ADM report found 75% of millennials interested in trying blended meats.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Demand evidence favors hybrid products, a tailwind for blended SKUs at incumbents like Tyson and Perdue and their suppliers.

insights.claim: Impossible's former CEO Peter McGuinness told the Wall Street Journal in 2025 that the brand has struggled to win consumers and suggested a hybrid burger could bridge the gap. Even the flagship plant-based company is admitting the limits of a fully plant-based approach.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Expect plant-based players to pivot toward hybrid products or ingredient partnerships with meat companies.

insights.claim: Blended-meat startups find that marketing on pleasure works and marketing on environmental or health benefits does not. Beef and mushrooms share umami glutamates, which is why the pairing tastes good. A school nutrition official deliberately avoids saying 'mushroom' because students would skip the dish.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Winning alt-protein brands will be stealth or taste-led, so impact claims are not a demand driver.

insights.locator: One major insight for all these upstarts

insights.claim: BMC Ingredients ferments the fungus Neurospora crassa on starch in a brewery-like process that yields a fibrous, meat-like protein in about four hours. Shapiro calls it among the most efficient ways to produce protein on Earth.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Fast fermentation cycles make mycelium a scalable ingredient platform, an alt-protein angle that sells to incumbents.

insights.claim: Joyn targets food service rather than retail: K-12 and college cafeterias and stadiums, because food eaten away from home is more than half of US food spending. Its 50/Cut blend is priced 5-15% below beef.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Selling at a discount to institutions with sustainability goals is a cleaner adoption path than winning over consumers at retail.
insights.locator: Joyn also sees its path forward

insights.claim: Joyn's 50/Cut meatball scored 92% approval among students in a Cane Bay High School taste test. It is now on school menus in seven states, and Cane Bay buys 200 cases at a time with 150 meatballs per case. Blended products are also in distributor catalogs such as Sysco's.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Getting into school and broadline distribution channels gives blended meat real volume.
insights.locator: The 50/Cut meatball is on the menu

insights.claim: Plantega founder Nil Zacharias doubts market forces alone will drive the shift. He says the backlash against ultra-processed plant-based foods disproves the belief that meat-tasting, cost-matched products will simply win, and expects blended meat's main impact to be in institutional dining like schools and health care.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Expect a ceiling on blended meat in retail, with institutional procurement as the main volume driver.

themes.theme: Bridge strategy and imperfect climate math

insights.claim: Nectar's Caroline Cotto compares blended meat to a hybrid car: it builds demand for fully plant-based ingredients that do not yet scale, bringing their costs down, so it serves both short- and long-term goals.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Hybrid volume may fund the ingredient scale-up that eventually makes fully plant-based products cost-competitive.
insights.quote: s. “So it’s both a short- and a long-term appro

insights.claim: A life-cycle analysis commissioned by Joyn shows the 50/Cut burger has half the greenhouse-gas footprint of a beef patty. Based on company claims, that is about five times the footprint of an Impossible or Beyond burger, so climate advocates will have to accept trading per-unit purity for adoption.
insights.speaker: Meghan McCarron
insights.so_what: Per-unit impact is worse than plant-based, but reach is far greater, so judge climate impact on total volume displaced.
